blocks.text: Imagine a world where computers can automatically prove mathematical theorems. How do they do it? The key lies in resolution and automated reasoning.

blocks.markdown: In this lesson, we will explore the concept of resolution in propositional logic, a fundamental technique used in automated reasoning systems. Resolution is a rule of inference that allows us to derive a contradiction from a set of clauses, thereby proving the unsatisfiability of the set. This method is central to automated theorem proving and logic programming.

blocks.title: Resolution Rule
blocks.text: The resolution rule is a single inference rule used in propositional logic. It states that given two clauses, \( C_1 = (A \lor B) \) and \( C_2 = (\neg A \lor C) \), we can infer the clause \( (B \lor C) \).

blocks.markdown: The resolution rule is applied to pairs of clauses that contain complementary literals. A literal is a propositional variable or its negation. The goal is to eliminate the complementary literals and combine the remaining parts of the clauses.

blocks.title: Applying the Resolution Rule
blocks.prompt: Apply the resolution rule to the clauses \( C_1 = (P \lor Q) \) and \( C_2 = (\neg P \lor R) \).

steps.text: Identify the complementary literals in \( C_1 \) and \( C_2 \).
The complementary literals are \( P \) and \( \neg P \).
Apply the resolution rule to eliminate \( P \) and \( \neg P \).

blocks.markdown: Resolution is particularly powerful in proving propositional entailments by refutation. The idea is to show that the negation of the desired conclusion, when added to the premises, leads to a contradiction.

blocks.title: Proving Entailment by Refutation
blocks.prompt: Prove that \( P \land (P \rightarrow Q) \models Q \) using resolution.

steps.text: Convert the premises and the negation of the conclusion into CNF (Conjunctive Normal Form).
Add the negation of the conclusion to the premises.
Apply resolution to \( P \) and \( (\neg P \lor Q) \).
Apply resolution to \( Q \) and \( \neg Q \).

blocks.answer: The empty clause \( \bot \) indicates a contradiction, proving the entailment.

blocks.title: Automated Provers and Clauses
blocks.text: Automated provers work with clauses because they simplify the search for contradictions. Clauses in CNF allow for systematic application of the resolution rule, making the process efficient and mechanizable.

blocks.markdown: Resolution is a complete method for propositional logic, meaning it can derive any logical consequence from a set of clauses. However, it is not directly applicable to arbitrary formulae, which is why conversion to CNF is necessary.

points: Resolution is a rule of inference used to derive contradictions from clauses.
Propositional entailment can be proved by refutation using resolution.
Automated provers use clauses in CNF to efficiently apply the resolution rule.
